newsitem.title: UK: BBA proposes euroLIBOR as benchmark from 1999.
newsitem.headline: BBA proposes euroLIBOR as benchmark from 1999.

text.p: The British Bankers' Association (BBA) said on Thursday it proposed a BBA euroLIBOR interest reference rate as a benchmark, replacing its EcuLIBOR from January 1, 1999.

"The BBA sponsors BBA LIBOR, the benchmark now used throughout the world's capital and derivatives markets," it said in a statement. It said its 300 plus member banks represented a broad cross section of national and international activity.
-- participating national currency LIBOR rates should be the same as those for euroLIBOR,
-- sterling interest calculations should remain unchanged if Britain stays outside a single European currency,
-- interest should be calulated using actual number of days divided by 360,
-- interest should accrue two business days after trade date
-- euroLIBOR should be available on all TARGET business days (so British holidays no longer affect global money markets).
"The new BBA euroLIBOR benchmark will preserve existing contracts based on LIBOR globally," it said.

"This will address market practitioners' concerns about continuity and will respond to international demand for a benchmark in the new currency to complement the eurodollar and euroyen LIBORs and replace the current ecuLIBOR," it said.
The BBA said regardless of Britain's status in Europe, a BBA euroLIBOR would be a key element in promoting liquidity and winning global acceptance for the new currency.
